newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serb hardliners expel Plavsic for party.
newsitem.headline: Serb hardliners expel Plavsic for party.

text.p: Bosnian Serb hardliners have expelled President Biljana Plavsic from the ruling SDS party and asked to turn over power to Vice-President Dragoljub Mirjanic, the Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA said on Sunday.
The decision to remove Plavsic was unanimous following her her threat to arrest former president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic for corruption.
She has also angered Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic by public identifying him as the guiding force behind Serb nationalism in Bosnia despite his denials of responsibility for the 1992-95 war.

The move against Plavsic risked splitting the Bosnian Serb entity in two, with rival governments in the northern town of Banja Luka where she is based and Pale, the hardliners' stronghold outside Sarajeveo to the south.
Her accusations have tapped unexpectedly strong public support among ordinary Bosnian Serbs, many of them living at subsistence levels in contrast with the wealth flaunted by Karadzic and his allies.
hardliners have accused Plavsic of being too cooperative with international mediators who also want to arrest Karadzic and other accused Bosnian Serbs for trial by the U.N. war crimes tribunal.
Their fears have hardened since British troops captured a war crimes suspect in the northern town of Prijedor this month and shot dead another who resisted arrest.
NATO units mounted an unusual show of force near Karadzic's heavily-guarded Pale home on Saturday

Peacekeepers and international observers have been the target of a series of minor retaliatory explosions, the latest of which occurred in Banja Luka last night. No injuries were reported in the two blasts.

The decision to expel Plavsic from the party brings the conflict to a head after earlier attempts by nationalist leaders to seek a compromise over her attempts to dissolve parliament and call fresh elections.
The dispute was suspended while the Bosnian Serb constitutional ruled on the legality of Plavsic's action.
Political sources said her continued attacks on Karadzic and his allies convinced them there was no point in waiting longer.
